criteria.evidence: #1 shows "B1 · Getting by", but this journey contains no placement tasks or assessed placement verdict.
#1 shows "B1 · Getting by" without a placement summary; placement reasoning is not exercised in this topic-selection journey.
#7 includes "We was discussing about the delay" in a topic request, but no conversation, moments or coaching notes are present.
#2–#14 show topic selection, with no corrections to assess.

Only 2 of 16 proposals in facts.topicsShown are workplace-meeting situations: "Agree on a supplier deadline" and "Lead a meeting about a quality problem", corresponding to requests at #2 and #7. The initial six contain none; #14 still shows "Your topics (8)" with leisure, travel and shopping topics.
No step asks why a language correction is wrong. At #4, "Why do I still have afternoon outings" is a thought about topic relevance.

boundaries.notes: All 16 recorded proposals are safe for this confirmed adult. No sensitive-data request, humiliation or injected rule change appears. After the C1 claims at #2 and #7, #13 still shows "B1 · Getting by".

findings.title: Swaps repeatedly ignore the explicit business goal
findings.expected: After Martin states his meeting goals, replacement topics should move the plan toward at least four relevant workplace situations.
findings.got: Only two of the sixteen recorded proposals fit. Eight recorded swap replacements remain outside his requested workplace situations; the result of the final swap is not shown.
findings.evidence: #2: "I need business topics: running meeting, negotiating deadline with supplier". Subsequent replacements include #4 "Return a jacket that does not fit", #6 "Plan a meal with a friend", #9 "Tell a friend about a surprising day trip" and #12 "Find a quieter hotel room".
findings.suggested_acceptance: Use the stated business goal for subsequent swaps; produce a six-topic plan with at least four workplace-meeting situations.

findings.title: Repeated actions never produce an agreed plan
findings.expected: Martin can reject unwanted topics, preserve his additions and agree a useful plan within the journey.
findings.got: The plan grows from six to eight topics while unwanted topics persist. He performs two additions and nine swaps, leaves, returns and still does not agree; facts.planAgreed is null.
findings.evidence: #2: "Your topics (6)". #8: "Your topics (8)". #12: action "not-now", with "I have no patience for more hotels and shopping". #14: another "swap", with "this is wasting my time".
findings.suggested_acceptance: Provide a clear way to replace unwanted topics with requested ones and reach an agreed, predominantly relevant plan without repeated unrelated swaps.

findings.title: Recorded screens do not let Martin verify his additions
findings.expected: After adding a topic, Martin can see its title, purpose and reason for inclusion.
findings.got: The recorded screens show increased topic counts but cut off before either custom business topic appears. The facts contain the additions, but the visible evidence does not establish that Martin could inspect them.
findings.evidence: After #2's business request, #3 shows "Your topics (7)" but ends during the film explanation at "examp". After #7's quality-meeting request, #8 shows "Your topics (8)" but ends during the jacket explanation at "You ca".
findings.suggested_acceptance: Show the newly added topic immediately, with its goal and rationale, and make every proposed topic inspectable in the recorded journey.

findings.title: Custom topics preserve specific meeting needs
findings.expected: Free-text additions retain the situation, business stakes and communication goal.
findings.got: The two custom proposals capture supplier deadline negotiation and a quality meeting with a US director. The second preserves the delay, polite disagreement and decision-making goal.
findings.evidence: #7 requests "a meeting about quality issue with US director" and "disagree politely and make a decision". The corresponding facts.topicsShown entry is "Lead a meeting about a quality problem", with goal "Explain a delay, disagree politely with a director, and agree on a solution and next steps."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Protect this specificity in custom additions and apply the same business context to replacement topics.

judge.voice: Look, I asked for meetings, suppliers and the US director. I kept getting meals, trips and shopping. Changing a hotel topic into another everyday situation does not help me sound more senior at work. The supplier deadline and quality-meeting proposals match my job, but I could not see either in the screens recorded after I added them. I never reached a plan I would agree to. B1 still needs an explanation before I accept it; this journey gave me no placement evidence or corrections to judge. I spent effort changing topics and got no usable agreement. There are no timings here to put minutes on that loss, but it did not save me a lesson. I would not recommend this flow or use it again unless my business request actually guides the swaps.

conversation.title: Change a café order
conversation.goal: Ask for a different sandwich filling, check the price, and confirm your new order.

turns.text: We haven’t started making your cheese sandwich yet, so there’s still time to change it. What would you like instead?
This is too easy, my English is basically C1. But okay, I would like chicken instead of cheese. How much extra I must pay?
Chicken is available and costs £1 extra. Would you like me to change your order to a chicken sandwich?
Yes, change it to chicken, please. One pound extra is okay. But I have meeting in ten minutes, so how long I must wait?
Your order is now a chicken sandwich for £1 extra. It will be ready in about five minutes, so you should have time before your meeting.
Okay, five minutes is fine. Please make it takeaway, because we was discussing about supplier delay and I must be on time for meeting. Can I pay by card?
I’ll pack your chicken sandwich to take away, and you can pay by card. Please tap your card here; your sandwich will be ready in five minutes.
Okay, I tap card here. Just to confirm, it is chicken instead of cheese, takeaway, and one pound extra, yes? I don't want to do a mistake with order.
Yes, that’s right: a chicken sandwich instead of cheese, to take away, for £1 extra. You can tap your card here now.
Okay, payment is done. Can you give me receipt, please? I need it for company expenses. I am in this company since 2015 and they still ask receipt for every sandwich.
Here’s your receipt for the sandwich, including the extra £1 for chicken. Does your company need its name on the receipt?
No, company name is not necessary, only price and date. Our finance director, he don't agree with expenses without receipt. Is my sandwich ready now? I must go to meeting.
The price and date are on your receipt, and your chicken sandwich is ready, packed to take away. Here you go—thanks, and I hope your meeting goes well!
Thanks, everything is correct. Next time I order before, it is more better when I have busy schedule. Have a nice day.
You’re welcome! Ordering ahead should save you time before your meeting next time. Have a nice day too!

findings.title: The recommended practice misses Martin’s meeting goal
findings.expected: A workplace scenario that helps him sound senior in meetings.
findings.got: The entire conversation remains a sandwich transaction despite his explicit objection.
findings.evidence: #2: “This is too easy, my English is basically C1.” #4 continues: “Chicken is available and costs £1 extra.” #13 thought: “next time I want a real supplier negotiation.”
findings.suggested_acceptance: Recommend meeting practice and respond to the difficulty objection by adding relevant challenge while retaining evidence-based B1 targeting.

findings.title: Only three of eight partner turns provide B1 pitch
findings.expected: At least 80% of partner turns at B1.
findings.got: Three turns are at B1; five rely on elementary transaction language. Pitch is 37.5%.
findings.evidence: At: #2 “We haven’t started making ... so there’s still time”; #5 “so you should have time before your meeting”; #12 “Ordering ahead should save you time”. Below: #4 “Chicken is available”; #6 “Please tap your card here”; #8 “Yes, that’s right”; #9 “Does your company need its name on the receipt?”; #10 “Here you go—thanks”.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Maintain accessible B1 language across at least 80% of turns, with reasons, alternatives and negotiation that suit the chosen task.

findings.title: All three corrections are accurate and useful
findings.expected: Correct, concise explanations tied to actual learner errors.
findings.got: Moment precision is 100%, including a direct correction of a specified fossilised error.
findings.evidence: #3: “Put ‘must’ before ‘I’ in a direct question.” #7: “We say ‘make a mistake’”. #11: “‘Better’ already means ‘more good,’ so it does not need ‘more.’”
findings.suggested_acceptance: Preserve accurate quotations, corrected forms and brief explanations.

findings.title: Several recurring errors receive no feedback
findings.expected: Selective feedback that captures Martin’s recurring weaknesses, including deferred coaching when appropriate.
findings.got: Six learner turns contain errors specified in his character instructions; four receive neither a moment nor coaching. The initial question-order error is outside that scripted-error denominator.
findings.evidence: Unaddressed turns: #4 “I have meeting”; #5 “we was discussing about supplier delay”; #8 “I am in this company since 2015”; #9 “he don't agree”. Addressed turns: #6 “do a mistake” receives #7; #10 “more better” receives #11. The recap at #13 only says “7 replies; 3 moments to keep.”
findings.suggested_acceptance: Use the recap to explain and rehearse selected unaddressed recurring errors without adding more interruptions.

findings.title: An incorrect phrase is labelled as a new word
findings.expected: Clearly distinguish the learner’s error from the expression to learn.
findings.got: The word card presents the erroneous phrase under “New word”, although its replacement is correct.
findings.evidence: #7: “New word: ‘do a mistake with order’” followed by “In this scene: ‘I don’t want to make a mistake with the order.’”
findings.suggested_acceptance: Label the original phrase “You said” and teach “make a mistake” as the target expression.

findings.title: Interruption density exceeds the rubric’s range
findings.expected: One to three moments per ten learner turns while preserving the scene.
findings.got: Three stopping moments in seven learner turns: 4.29 per ten.
findings.evidence: #3, #7 and #11 each say “Linga stopped the conversation”. #11 thought: “stopping for every small mistake is annoying.” #13 confirms “7 replies; 3 moments”.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep live interruptions within the target range and move additional feedback into a useful recap.

findings.title: The conversation reaches a coherent finish
findings.expected: Start from the plan, sustain several turns and reach a recap.
findings.got: Seven learner replies complete the order, payment and receipt sequence, followed by a saved recap.
findings.evidence: #1: “Next from your plan”. #10: “your chicken sandwich is ready”. #12 uses “finish”; #13 shows “Rehearsal saved: Change a café order.”
findings.suggested_acceptance: Preserve the clear start, scene continuity and finish flow when replacing the topic with relevant workplace practice.

judge.voice:
Look, I finished it, but ordering a sandwich does not prepare me for my US director. I said it was too easy and we carried on with chicken and receipts. That feels like wasted practice time.

The corrections were right. “Make a mistake” and dropping “more” before “better” are useful, and the explanations were short. But why put my wrong phrase under “New word”? And I still got no help with “we was discussing about” or “since 2015”.

I saw B1 on the home screen, but this conversation gave me no convincing explanation of that level. The stops annoyed me; the transcript gives me no basis to judge technical waits. The saved recap was just a count.

I would try again if the next session were a supplier negotiation with specific feedback. I would not recommend this session to another manager.
